newsitem.title: USA: NY Gov signs 1997 budget with $280 mln of tax cuts.
newsitem.headline: NY Gov signs 1997 budget with $280 mln of tax cuts.

text.p: New York Gov. George Pataki said he signed into law the state's approximately $66 billion budget for the 1997 fiscal year, which includes new tax cuts that will total about $280 million when fully in place.

Pataki trumpeted the tax cuts included in the new budget, which was not agreed until 104 days after it was due April 1. In prepared remarks released Friday, he said they reduced the tax burden on New Yorkers to the lowest level since 1972.
The budget moves forward with $2.3 billion in existing tax cuts, including a second phase of $1.8 billion in working family tax cuts and $300 million from phasing out business tax surcharges.
Spending from the General Fund will total nearly $500 million less than in 1994-95, Pataki said, referring to the last year of former Gov. Mario Cuomo's Administration.

The budget bills signed so far include workers' compensation reforms, expected to cut costs by 25 percent or about $1 billion, and plan to let hospitals negotiate rates with providers instead of having the state set them.
"These policy successes are successes for all New Yorkers and will help to create jobs and economic freedom and continue the renewal this state has been experiencing," Pataki said.
